stories.title: Morris Heights Seniors Housing Project Secures Permits
stories.excerpt: Permits have been approved for a new 10-story affordable senior housing development at 105 W. Tremont Ave. in the Morris Heights neighborhood of the Bronx. Developed by Crown Holdings in partnership with The Community Builders, one of the nation’s largest affordable housing organizations, the project will provide 95 Affordable Independent Residences forSeniors (AIRS) and form part of a broader neighborhood regeneration initiative in Morris Heights. Designed by Crown Architecture, the approximately 55,000-square-foot, 100-foot-tall building will bring housing and support services to a borough where demand for affordable homes outpaces supply. In addition to housing, residents will have access to onsite amenities and services that include community and recreational spaces, an outdoor patio and garden, consultation rooms, laundry facilities, bicycle storage and a 24-hour attended receptionThe project incorporates a strong sustainability agenda through its Passive House design standards. The all-electric building will also feature an approximately 1,800-square-foot rooftop solar array. The post Morris Heights Seniors Housing Project Secures Permits appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Crown Holdings & Community Builders secure permits for 95-unit affordable senior housing in Morris Heights, Bronx
10-story, 55,000 SF development at 105 W. Tremont Ave. addresses borough's undersupply of affordable homes
Passive House all-electric design with onsite services; project part of neighborhood regeneration initiative
stories.summary: Crown Holdings and The Community Builders have won permits for a new 95-unit affordable senior housing project in Morris Heights, the Bronx, a 55,000-square-foot, 10-story building incorporating Passive House standards and all-electric systems. The project responds to documented demand outpacing supply for affordable homes in the borough. It includes community spaces, services, and support amenities, and is part of a broader neighborhood regeneration effort.
stories.impact: Signals strong public-sector appetite for affordable senior housing in outer boroughs and de facto validation of demand fundamentals in underserved Bronx submarkets. The PILOT/subsidy stack and entitlement pathway demonstrate path-to-close for mission-driven developments; multifamily developers should monitor whether this unlocks pipeline velocity or land availability in Morris Heights and surrounding gentrifying Bronx corridors.

stories.title: Fully Leased Chula Vista Retail Fetches $30M
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $30.4-million sale of Terra Nova Plaza, a fully leased, 96,114-square-foot retail property positioned within a 301,000-square-foot regional shopping center in Chula Vista. Senior managing director Gleb Lvovich, managing director Daniel Tyner and senior managing director Geoff Tranchina. represented the seller, a global investment manager. Located at 390 E H St., Terra Nova Plaza sits within a high-performing grocery-anchored center. Dick’s Sporting Goods operates from a 44,477-square-foot space, while Floor & Decor occupies 51,637 square feet under long-term leases. Co-tenants within the larger center include Smart & Final, CVS, Marshalls, Chase Bank, Taco Bell, Jack In the Box and Shell. “The combination of long-term lease security, exceptional freeway visibility and proximity to one of the region’s most dynamic residential growth corridors made this an extremely compelling opportunity,” said Lvovich. “Chula Vista’s retail fundamentals remain strong with limited new supply and continued demand from quality tenants seeking high-traffic locations.” The post Fully Leased Chula Vista Retail Fetches $30M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Terra Nova Plaza, 96K SF retail in Chula Vista, CA, sells fully leased for $30.4M
Dick's Sporting Goods (44K SF) and Floor & Decor (51K SF) anchors on long-term leases
Broker cites limited new supply and proximity to dynamic residential growth corridor as driver
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets brokered the $30.4 million sale of Terra Nova Plaza, a 96,114-square-foot fully leased retail property in Chula Vista anchored by Dick's Sporting Goods and Floor & Decor. The property sits within a 301,000-square-foot regional shopping center with strong co-tenancy (Smart & Final, CVS, Chase, QSR). The broker highlighted limited new supply, high freeway visibility, and proximity to residential growth as investment drivers.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Retail-focused transaction; however, broker's emphasis on 'dynamic residential growth corridors' near Chula Vista may signal demographic tailwinds that could drive demand for apartment communities in the submarket if demographics and job growth are tracking.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Debt, Equity for Port Chester Multifamily Project
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. has arranged $147.5 million in debt and equity capitalization for the construction of 2 South Main, a 322-unit multifamily project in downtown Port Chester, NY. The sponsorship group is a joint venture between Hyperion, Winter Properties and AIP. The Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets team of Mo Beler, Jonathan Paine, Cory Elbaum, Jackson Irwin, and Dawson Jessee arranged the equity investment from Related Fund Management, while Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet and Stanley Cayre secured construction financing from Arbor Realty Trust. The project is in an Opportunity Zone and also benefits from a 20-year PILOT agreement. “The successful capitalization of 2 South Main demonstrates the continued demand for well-conceived housing developments that meet both market needs and community priorities,” said Beler. “We structured and sourced the project’s construction financing and equity investment while leveraging public-sector incentives. This enabled us to deliver a comprehensive capital solution that positions the development for long-term success and supports the continued growth of downtown Port Chester.” The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges Debt, Equity for Port Chester Multifamily Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop closes $147.5M debt and equity for 322-unit downtown Port Chester, NY multifamily project
Joint venture Hyperion/Winter Properties/AIP sources equity from Related Fund Management, construction debt from Arbor Realty Trust
Project qualifies for Opportunity Zone and 20-year PILOT agreement, enhancing feasibility and returns
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged $147.5 million in construction financing and equity for 2 South Main, a 322-unit multifamily development in downtown Port Chester, NY, led by a joint venture of Hyperion, Winter Properties, and AIP. Related Fund Management provided equity and Arbor Realty Trust provided construction debt. The project benefits from Opportunity Zone tax incentives and a 20-year PILOT agreement that materially reduced effective development cost.
stories.impact: Capital availability and tax incentive structuring remain robust for well-positioned multifamily projects in secondary markets with strong fundamentals. Port Chester's downtown trajectory and PILOT/OZ stack demonstrate how public incentives can unlock marginal sites; developers should prioritize Westchester submarkets with similar transit, entitlement, and public-sector support profiles for near-term starts.

stories.title: Barnes & Noble Opens New Store in Chicago
stories.excerpt: Barnes & Noble announced the upcoming opening of its newest bookstore in Chicago, Illinois. The new store is to open on State Street in The Loop, in the historic building that was once a flagship Borders Bookstore. More recently, the building was occupied by Old Navy. The store, located at 150 N State Street, is situated in the heart of downtown Chicago. It is the fourth new Barnes & Noble bookstore to open in the Chicagoland area this year, in addition to other locations in Skokie, Hyde Park, and Oak Park. The new Barnes & Noble bookstore will span more than 20,000 square feet.“We are delighted to restore this wonderful building as a home to a major bookstore,” said James Daunt, CEO of Barnes & Noble. “Returning to The Loop reinforces a significant commitment to Chicago, where we have now opened four new bookstores in the last year.” Barnes & Noble now has more than 720 bookstores. The post Barnes & Noble Opens New Store in Chicago appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Barnes & Noble opens 20K SF flagship at 150 N State Street in Chicago Loop (fourth new B&N in Chicagoland this year)
Occupies former Borders and Old Navy location; reflects CEO commitment to downtown retail revival
No specific multifamily demand signal embedded in announcement
stories.summary: Barnes & Noble opened a new 20,000-square-foot bookstore at 150 N State Street in Chicago's Loop, in a historic building that previously housed Borders and Old Navy. The opening is the fourth new Barnes & Noble in Chicagoland this year, signaling management's commitment to Chicago markets. CEO James Daunt framed the move as restoring a flagship location to a major downtown corridor.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Retail tenant commitment to Loop signals modest stabilization of downtown Chicago, but does not indicate demand drivers (employment, population migration, wage growth) that would materially impact apartment fundamentals or development activity in the submarket.

stories.title: TikTok Tells U.S. Employees to Return to Office 5 Days a Week
stories.excerpt: TikTok’s work-from-home era is scrolling to an end. The ByteDance-owned social media platform has instructed its U.S. employees to return to the office five days a week, sources told Business Insider. The change impacts the company’s hybrid employees that are currently allowed to work from home at least one day per week. TikTok alerted employees across several large divisions in December to expect a full office return in 2026, according to Insider, although certain teams, like TikTok’s e-commerce division, resumed five-day office attendance more than a year ago. TikTok employs thousands of U.S. employees across dozens of metro office locations, including its Culver City headquarters in Greater Los Angeles, and a seven-floor spread at the Durst Organization’s One Five One tower in Manhattan’s Times Square. TikTok earlier this month announced the closure of its 250-person Nashville office, however, just two years since opening. Return-to-office policies have been gaining ground across the country and across industries this year, Commercial Observer previously reported. U.S. office visits rose 6 percent year-over-year in the first half of 2026, and achieved the narrowest first-half gap from pre-pandemic levels thus far. The return-to-office wave has continued to buoy post-pandemic office leasing in cities like New York, where returning demand has driven rents to record highs this year. TikTok’s move to reign in work-from-home follows similar moves by its competitors Instagram and Amazon. Amazon’s office workers returned for five-day work weeks nearly two years ago, while other large technology companies, like YouTube and Patreon, have maintained their hybrid schedules. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: TikTok mandates full return-to-office 5 days/week for U.S. hybrid employees starting 2026
Impacts thousands of employees across metro offices: Culver City HQ (Greater Los Angeles) and seven-floor spread at One Five One tower (Times Square, Manhattan)
Company closed Nashville 250-person office in December after just two years, signaling consolidation and retrenchment
stories.summary: TikTok has instructed U.S. employees to return to the office five days per week effective 2026, ending its hybrid work policy. The company operates thousands of employees across multiple metro locations, including its Culver City headquarters in Greater Los Angeles and a seven-floor presence at the Durst Organization's One Five One in Times Square, Manhattan. The move follows TikTok's closure of its Nashville office (250 staff) in December after just two years.
stories.impact: Mixed signal for multifamily. Full RTO mandate supports office leasing in LA and Manhattan, potentially stabilizing Class-A office assets and reducing vacancy-driven repricing pressure in those submarkets—which historically constrains multifamily development financing and neighborhood commercial stabilization. However, Nashville office exit signals that secondary markets face headwinds from consolidation and potential remote-work persistence in tech; developers should avoid speculative multifamily concentration tied to TikTok-type employers in secondary office markets.

stories.title: Spirit Halloween Inks Seasonal Lease for 10K SF in Medford
stories.excerpt: The Hamilton Company has leased approximately 10,000 square feet to Sprit Halloween at 55 Riverside Ave. in Medford, MA, which formerly housed a CVS. The retailer will open more than 1,550 seasonal locations this year across strip malls and shopping centers throughout North America, signaling the start of the Halloween season. “We are excited to have Spirit Halloween in our building in Medford,” said Jameson Brown, chairman and CEO of The Hamilton Company. “They have an impressive history that spans more than four decades as America’s leading Halloween-themed retailer.” Spirit Halloween’s in-house counsel represented the retailer during the leasing negotiations. The Hamilton Company was represented by Carol Rash, The Hamilton Company’s Director of Commercial Property & Asset Management. “Seasonal retail or ‘pop-up’ stores are growing total revenue and market presence at a significant pace each year,” said Rash. “Spirit Halloween is a category leader, and we’re thrilled with their occupancy of 55 Riverside Ave.” The post Spirit Halloween Inks Seasonal Lease for 10K SF in Medford appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Spirit Halloween signs 10K SF seasonal lease at 55 Riverside Ave. in Medford, MA (former CVS location)
Retailer opening 1,550+ seasonal locations across North America; lease demonstrates retail landlord demand for pop-up tenants
Transaction reflects shift toward high-velocity seasonal retail filling vacant retail footprints
stories.summary: The Hamilton Company leased approximately 10,000 square feet at 55 Riverside Ave. in Medford, MA to Spirit Halloween, a former CVS location. Spirit Halloween is opening more than 1,550 seasonal locations across North America this year. The broker noted that seasonal retail is growing revenue and market presence significantly year-over-year.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Pop-up retail activity can temporarily mask underlying retail vacancy and supply-chain stress, but does not generate durable tenant demand or stabilize neighborhood real estate values. Seasonal retail lease-ups may obscure true retail fundamentals; multifamily developers relying on neighborhood retail vitality should not read Spirit Halloween activity as a demand signal.

stories.title: Blackstone Snaps Up Ken Griffin’s 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach for $86M
stories.excerpt: Billionaire Ken Griffin just parted ways with his last remaining retail property on Worth Avenue in Palm Beach, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Blackstone Real Estate has agreed to acquire the three-story office and retail building at 125 Worth Avenue, owned by Griffin since 2023, for $86 million in an all-cash deal, sources familiar with the trade said. Griffin previously bought the roughly 50,000-square-foot property from Dreyfuss Management and Frisbie Group for $83 million in 2023. “High-street retail continues to experience strong fundamentals, and Palm Beach represents one of the highest performing luxury retail markets in North America,” Elena Clarfield, principal at Blackstone Real Estate, told Commercial Observer. Indeed, as a retail corridor, the world famous Worth Avenue enjoys extreme scarcity when it comes to supply, coupled with soaring demand from a deluge of high-income residents into Palm Beach. Limited supply has also driven up property valuations in the prestigious area, evidenced by Acadia Realty Trust’s March 2026 acquisition of 225 Worth Avenue, leased to Gucci, for $43 million, or more than $4,329 per square foot. Blackstone declined to comment further but sources said the firm now intends to renovate the property, upgrading both the retail and office components to better align them with the continued evolution of Worth Avenue, a high-scale shopping district that’s home to several luxury tenants including Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Ferragamo and Van Cleef & Arpels. Representatives for Griffin could not immediately be reached for comment. The transaction represents Griffin’s second disposition on Worth Avenue in under a year. Last November, the billionaire sold his 48,578-square-foot property at 151 Worth Avenue to the family of GoldenTree Asset Management financier Steven Tananbaum, Commercial Observer reported at the time. bullets: Blackstone acquires 125 Worth Avenue, Palm Beach for $86M all-cash (Ken Griffin sold after two-year hold at ~$3M gain)
50K SF luxury retail/office property reflects extreme scarcity and soaring high-income resident demand on Worth Avenue
Broker cites 'highest performing luxury retail markets in North America' and supply constraints driving valuations
stories.summary: Blackstone Real Estate acquired the three-story, 50,000-square-foot office and retail property at 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach for $86 million in an all-cash transaction from billionaire Ken Griffin, who held it for less than three years. The broker highlighted Worth Avenue's extreme supply scarcity and strong demand from high-income residents moving to Palm Beach as drivers of the asset's valuation.
stories.impact: Signals continued wealth migration into Palm Beach and extreme pricing power in ultra-luxury real estate. While this transaction is retail-focused, the underlying demographic story—high-net-worth individuals relocating to Palm Beach—directly correlates with demand for luxury multifamily (especially Class-A rental and condo-conversion inventory). Developers should prioritize oceanfront and downtown Palm Beach multifamily sites and expect continued pricing power in luxury rental; however, retail-office hybrid assets may face obsolescence pressure if retail foot-traffic concentrates narrowly on Worth Avenue versus mixed-use neighborhoods.

stories.title: Fund Administrator Hanover Park Inks 19K-SF Deal at 387 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator is moving its headquarters to TF Cornerstone’s 387 Park Avenue South, Commercial Observer has learned. Hanover Park signed a 19,269-square-foot lease on the entire 10th floor of the NoMad property, marking its fifth office move in two years, according to CEO Chris Hladczuk. The firm’s most recent office address is listed on its website as 115 East 23rd Street. TF Cornerstone did not immediately provide the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Existing tenants are choosing to expand here and new companies are choosing to locate here,” Joe Lanzilotta, director of commercial asset management at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “The property continues to outperform the market as a destination for growing businesses.” It is unclear who represented the tenant in the transaction, but Cushman & Wakefield’s Ethan Silverstein handled negotiations on behalf of the landlord in the deal signed in July. It’s unclear who represented the tenant. “The combination of TF Cornerstone’s long-term investment, highly efficient 20,000-square-foot floor plates and premier NoMad location continues to resonate with tenants,” Silverstein said in a statement. “The recent leasing activity demonstrates that companies are prioritizing best-in-class buildings, and with one full floor becoming available this fall, the property remains well positioned to meet continued demand.” Other recent deals in the 230,000-square-foot building at the corner of Park Avenue South and East 27th Street include a lease for marketing firm PMG Worldwide, which expanded from the second to third floor in May and brought its total footprint there to 38,744 square feet, according to TF Cornerstone. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hanover Park (AI-driven fund administrator) leases 19.3K SF floor at TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Avenue South, NoMad
Tenant completing fifth office move in two years; Midtown South average asking rent $85.73/SF in Q2 2026
TF Cornerstone broker reports existing tenant expansions and new company interest, property outperforming market
stories.summary: Hanover Park, an artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator, signed a 19,269-square-foot lease for the entire 10th floor at TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Avenue South in NoMad, marking its fifth office move in two years. The average asking rent for Midtown South office space was $85.73 per square foot in Q2 2026. The landlord reported strong tenant demand and expansions at the property.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Office tenant churn and repeated relocations suggest limited workplace stability or real estate commitment in tech/finance services; however, TF Cornerstone's reported outperformance in Midtown South may indicate that mixed-use neighborhoods with restaurant/retail density are attracting tenant activity. Developers should monitor whether office leasing strength in NoMad spills over to support ground-floor retail and foot-traffic for adjacent or nearby multifamily projects.

stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Ritz-Carlton Portland With $141M C-PACE Loan
stories.excerpt: A New York lender is more than ready for a Portland hospitality resurgence. Ready Capital, which assumed full ownership of the The Ritz-Carlton Portland mixed-use project following a foreclosure in July 2025, just secured $141 million of commercial property accessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the 35-story tower, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the C-PACE loan for the 2023-completed Block 216 Tower development that features a 251-key hotel, 131 condominium units and 159,000 square feet of office space. Construction of the Ritz-Carlton-Portland, the Marriott’s brand’s first hotel in the Pacific Northwest, commenced in 2019 before encountering delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuing struggles to the city’s economy. Jared Schlosser, head of credit originations at Peachtree Group, said condo units at the property have sold at a healthy pace and the hotel is well positioned for success as one of the newest lodging offerings in the Portland region. “It’s the nicest hotel up there and that pocket of Portland is revitalizing,” Schlosser told CO. “I think there’s probably more tailwinds ahead versus headwinds for Portland.” Schlosser added that C-PACE debt was conducive for the recap since as a newer building it was developed under “stringent” building codes with much of the project eligible for retroactive financing. He noted that the deal marks Peachtree’s second largest loan. Ready Capital set the stage for owning The Ritz-Carlton Portland when it acquired a prior construction loan on the development valued at more than $500 million through a 2022 merger with Mosaic Real Estate Investors. The lender manages the property in partnership with Lincoln Property Company. Ready Capital did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ready Capital (post-foreclosure owner) secures $141M C-PACE refinancing for Ritz-Carlton Portland Block 216 Tower
Mixed-use 35-story: 251-key hotel, 131 condos, 159K SF office; completed 2023, encountered COVID/economic delays
C-PACE financing structure suggests institutional appetite to stabilize Portland hospitality/residential despite pandemic legacy headwinds
stories.summary: Ready Capital, which acquired the Ritz-Carlton Portland following foreclosure in July 2025, secured $141 million in C-PACE debt to recapitalize Block 216 Tower, a 35-story mixed-use project completed in 2023 featuring 251 hotel keys, 131 condominiums, and 159,000 square feet of office space. The project experienced construction delays due to COVID-19 and subsequent economic challenges in Portland. Peachtree Group originated the C-PACE loan and cited healthy condo sales velocity and strong hotel positioning.
stories.impact: Signals lender willingness to recapitalize mixed-use projects in secondary markets post-distress, underpinned by C-PACE financing vehicles that reduce cost of capital. However, foreclosure and extended stabilization timeline reflect Portland's hospitality/real estate challenges (pandemic, office vacancy, economic weakness). For multifamily developers: mixed-use residential-hotel projects in Portland face extended lease-up timelines and capital-structure risk; consider single-purpose multifamily over mixed-use in secondary markets with uncertain office and hospitality recovery.

stories.title: Office Furniture Manufacturer Haworth Renews 30K SF at SL Green’s 125 Park Avenue
stories.excerpt: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth is staying seated at 125 Park Avenue. Haworth has signed a 10-year lease renewal for its 30,365-square-foot office and showroom space at the 25-story Midtown office building, landlord SL Green Realty announced Wednesday. The company, which manufactures and sells high-end, ergonomic office seating and workspaces, has been a tenant in the property, also known as the Pershing Square Building, for more than a decade. The firm, which did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, previously renewed its lease for the same space back in 2015, CO reported at the time. The asking rent was $100 per square foot. SL Green was represented in-house in this deal, while Haworth was represented by Ethan Silverstein and Amy Zhen from Cushman & Wakefield. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “We are proud to extend our valued relationship with Haworth at 125 Park Avenue,” Steven Durels, executive vice president and director of leasing and real property at SL Green, said in a statement. “The building’s proximity to Grand Central Terminal and our new lobby and elevator cab renovation have helped maintain 99 percent occupancy.” SL Green acquired 125 Park Avenue in 2010 for $330 million, according to property records. The building sits across the street from Grand Central Terminal on Park Avenue and East 42nd Street. Other tenants in the building include banking and investment firm TD Securities and real estate brokerage Newmark. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Haworth renews 30.4K SF office/showroom for 10 years at SL Green's 125 Park Avenue (Pershing Square), Midtown
Tenant (office furniture manufacturer) renews for second consecutive decade, signaling stability in Class-A Midtown office space
No distress; renewal with existing 10+ year relationship reflects ongoing demand for premium office showroom space
stories.summary: Haworth, an office furniture manufacturer and seller, signed a 10-year lease renewal for 30,365 square feet of office and showroom space at SL Green's 125 Park Avenue (Pershing Square Building) in Midtown Manhattan. The company has been a tenant for more than a decade and previously renewed in 2015. SL Green highlighted the building's proximity to Grand Central Terminal and recent lobby upgrades.
stories.impact: Modest positive signal for Manhattan office demand, but limited relevance to multifamily development. Long-term renewal by a stable, non-tech tenant in Class-A Midtown suggests institutional occupiers remain committed to premium office space; this reduces downside cap-rate expansion risk for office-anchored mixed-use projects in Midtown. Multifamily developers should note that 125 Park Avenue's renewal strength may reflect Grand Central proximity and transit/walkability fundamentals—factors that also support higher-density residential demand and rental pricing in Midtown East submarkets.
